main_text.p: Κεχύμβη, braffica, faftidium parere folita, unde proverbium, Crambe bis cofta: Græci dicunt; Δὶς κεχύμβη δὶς αὐτὸ. Hinc puto Anglicum, to cramme. Alioquin ex χοῖω, unde κεχορτιμένος, fatiatus, ducerem. Facit tamen ad priorem rationem, quòd Bœotos κεχύμβω, pro χοῖει dixiffe, notat ex Athenæo. Euftathius.

Κάμπτω, curvo, inflecto. Anglis, to crumpe. Unde, crump-legg'd: crump-shouldred, &c. to crumble aliud, quod ex crumme, mica. Καμπή, flexura, curvamen. flexus artuum, articulus, nodus, suffrago. Angl. crampe, spasmus. Krimpen, Belgis, contrahere, quæ propior origo merito censeatur. Sed hoc ipsum ex Græco κάμπτειν, cùm flectendo res contrahantur: aut certè ex χείμπτω, appropinquare facio, admoveo. Sed & τὸ crtpple, mancus, claudus; ab eodem, ni fallor, κάμπτω.
Κρώβυλοι, cincinni, crines intorti: puerorum proprie. Hodie, curled bapre: olim crul, ut ex Chaucero notatum quibusdam. Sed & crocks olim pro cincinnis usurpatum notant iidem.

page.notes: Greek and Latin partly blurred; several Greek words uncertain and transcribed approximately. Bottom catchword is a Greek fragment, possibly a catchword.
